analysis: The only change in this PR is a documentation row added at head line 413 of docs/reference/configuration.md. It documents DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP, an operator-set environment variable for load-time shape warmup on ordinary EngineV2 slots. No executable code, key handling, attestation, coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), or encrypted prefix-cache storage code is changed. The row claims the warmup trains no rate or counter, is probe-gated and capped at 20 seconds per engine, and is forwarded to the LaunchAgent. The backing source files (ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift and the LaunchAgent passthrough) are not in the supplied evidence, so those claims are unverified and do not constitute a finding. Relevant threat IDs are T-010, T-029, T-028 and T-041, but none is materially touched. The warmup runs synthetic shape cells and probes at load, not consumer data, so it should not affect A-001 or the prefix-cache TTFT oracle. The review pass should confirm that the warmup uses synthetic inputs only and does not donate to the SSD prefix cache, and that the LaunchAgent passthrough allow-list change, if any, adds only this benign flag. The `always` and off values only alter startup latency. The surrounding base text in the supplied units is unchanged documentation and is not re-reported.
